passages.text: Say a female is adulterous and objectionable but will have the knack to treat her husband with apparent love and consideration and thus give no room for complaint as a wife, then he thinks he is happy. passages.text: Even among cruel or odd signs there is, and there must be great difference in producing the evil effects. When the Lagna of a girl falls in any one of them or Chandra occupies any one of these, her characteristics, will differ.
passages.summary: The book says the odd signs differ in their evil effects because they are ruled by different planets (Aries by Mars, Gemini by Mercury, Leo by the Sun, Libra by Venus, Sagittarius by Jupiter, Aquarius by Saturn), so a girl's characteristics will differ according to which of them holds her ascendant or Moon.

passages.chapterTitle: Characteristics of Girls
passages.text: The characteristics of girls all over the world are characterised by a surprising and wonderful variety and these are accounted for by the permutations and combinations of Rasis constellations, planets and the various states ascribed to these in different places. Take Aries. Kuja in its first degree is not the same as when he is in the second. Ravi in the first degree of Mesha is not the same as Ravi in the 10th or 30th degree of that sign. Similarly every planet in every sign has changes in nature in each degree and the Bhava or signification it occupies. These wonderful varieties of planets in degrees, Bhavas and signs account for the endless variety we find in the bad or good nature
passages.summary: The book says the great variety in girls' characteristics comes from the many combinations of signs, constellations, planets and their states. It explains that a planet acts differently in each degree of a sign and in each house it occupies, which accounts for the endless variety in good or bad nature. passages.text: The readers attention is drawn to certain facts in making predictions about the character of women. There are many delicacies which should be particularly noted. In the above paras the expression used is " if Chandra or Lagna " falls in so and so. Chandra and Lagna may fall in one and the same sign or each may fall in a different house.

passages.chapterTitle: Strength and Weakness of the Planets and Signs
passages.text: In all these cases predictions should be based on a careful analyses of the various sources of strength and weakness of the planets. If Mesha rises as the 7th Navamsa and is occupied by Guru, or if it rises with Sani in it or Kuja or any other planet the results will vary with the nature of the planet. Mesha Navamsa may rise as the 7th in Thula Lagna and Vrischika Navamsa will rise as the 7th in Vrishabha Lagna. In other Lagnas, Mesha and Vrischika will not rise as the 7th Navamsa. If Lagna falls in any sign, there must be some sign which occupies the house and some Navamsa must rise as the 7th. Out of the 7th house and the 7th Navamsa, find out which is stronger and ascribe the results to it. But in doing so, there will be a tinge of the 7th house as Navamsa, which is weaker. Suppose Kataka falls as 7th and is occupied by Kuja and Kataka Navamsa rises with Guru in it. Here it will be seen, that between the 7th house and the 7th Navamsa, the Navamsa is stronger, and the Rasi is weaker. The results for the 7th Navamsa should be predicted in preference to 7th Rasi. In all these cases great patience, laborious calculations, high deligence, and excellent analysing power should be brought to bear on the subject, in order to arrive at correct results. Haste, and want of patient labour, will bring the man and his noble science to ruin and disgrace.
passages.summary: The book says predictions must weigh the strength and weakness of the planets, and that the results depend on which planet occupies the 7th house or 7th Navamsa. The astrologer should judge whether the 7th house or the 7th Navamsa is stronger and give its results first, with a tinge of the weaker one, and the author warns that haste and lack of patient work bring the astrologer and the science into disgrace.

passages.chapterTitle: Beneficial Aspects and Conjunctions
passages.text: Full-moon and well associated Mercury are classed as benefics. But when the Moon is weak like on a New-moon day and Mercury with Rahu, Sani, Mars and Kethu, he is said to be evil. Here great differences must be made in the results. Suppose Kanya is Lagna with Budha and Sani and Meena as Lagna with them. The results will be and must be different. In Meena Budha is debilitated, and with Sani, he will give bad results. In Kanya he is exalted and with Sani he will give better results. Suppose in Kanya they are joined by Guru and so also in Meena, there will be difference in results. If Sukra joins them in Kanya or Meena the results will be quite different. In astrology, it is no joke to make correct predictions, for, the astrologer has to remember all such details, analyse them as best as he could, balance the conflicting evidence, combine theory and practice, use common sense and intelligence, study the environments of the parties, consider the local, the political, the social and the religious conditions and then, after summarising all these, draw reasonable conclusions and make predictions with care and caution.
passages.summary: The book explains that a full Moon and a well-associated Mercury count as benefics, while a weak Moon or a Mercury joined with malefics counts as malefic, and illustrates how the same planets give different results in Virgo and Pisces rising. It stresses that correct prediction requires weighing all such details, conflicting evidence, common sense and the person's circumstances before drawing careful conclusions.

passages.chapterTitle: Characteristics of the Twelve Signs
passages.text: I will now give the description and characteristics of girls born in the 12 different Rasis and these are to be taken with considerable modifications. For example, if a girl is born in Mesha without any planet or with Ravi, Chandra, Kuja, Budha, Guru, Sukra, Sani, Rahu or Kethu, in all these ten cases, the results will be necessarily different. This should be particularly borne in mind. But there will also be the general influences of the Rasi itself, which will be strongly or weakly marked according to the strength or weakness of the Rasi itself, its lord and the planets who are there and who aspect it. Kuja in Mesha will be its lord. Ravi in Mesha will have exaltation, Chandra will be in a friendly house. Budha will be emerging from debilitation and in an unfriendly sign. Guru will be in a friendly sign. Sukra will be in an enemy's house. Sani will be debilitated. Rahu will be powerful. Kethu will be weak. Therefore the results of a girl born in Mesha, vary according to the strength and weakness of these planets and Rasis. Then again we have double, trible, quadruple, multiple, sextile and separate combinations, each of which has its own strength and weakness. Therefore, when we give the results for Mesha, Vrishabha and so forth, the astrologers must be very careful, in making their predictions.
passages.summary: The book introduces descriptions of girls born in each of the 12 signs and warns that they must be modified by the planets in the sign, its lord and aspects. Using Mesha as an example, it notes how each planet fares there and urges astrologers to be very careful in predicting.

passages.chapterTitle: Characteristics of the Twelve Signs
passages.text: In judging of these characteristics the reader has to be careful. When the sign is powerful, well occupied, beneficially aspected and when its lord has good conjunctions and aspects then the characteristics sketched above will appear in full. But when the sign is weak and has evil conjunctions and aspects, its lord is not powerful then the results can only have general traces and not in full. One or two examples will suffice to explain what I mean.
passages.summary: The book says the sign descriptions show in full only when the sign and its lord are strong and well aspected; when they are weak or afflicted, only general traces appear.

passages.chapterTitle: Characteristics of the Twelve Signs
passages.text: Take Kataka. If it is occupied by Kuja, if its lord Moon is both New moon and debilitated in Vrischika then there will be faint traces of the characteristics represented by Kataka. But if Guru is there and Chandra is full and exalted then all the characteristics given for Cancer will be prominently visible. The task of an Astrologer if he wants to be honest and faithful to his science is not only taxing but also laborious. Sciences whatever they may be, are not for [?] fools or ignorant brains. Devotion, intelligence, patience and industry are wanted.
passages.summary: The book illustrates with Kataka: with Mars in it and a new, debilitated Moon, its traits show only faintly, but with Jupiter in it and a full, exalted Moon they show fully. It adds that honest astrology demands devotion, intelligence, patience and hard work.

passages.chapterTitle: Characteristics of the Twelve Signs
passages.text: When Chandra is in any particular sign, not aspected or conjoined by good or evil planets and the lord of the sign is powerful as has already been stated, then the characteristics detailed for that sign will be prominently seen. But when conjunctions and aspects are present and conflicting, then there will be traces of these results. We say a girl is handsome. In beauty there are any number of varieties and the judgments on beauty also vary according to the tastes of nations, manners, customs, social functions and aesthetic development. Habit also has great deal to do with our tastes and judgments. The darkest Negro, the Hottentot, the American, the Indian, the Aboriginals of India, the European and the Asiatic nations all have their own ideas of beauty.
passages.summary: The book says the Moon-sign traits show strongly when the Moon is unaspected and unconjoined and the sign's lord is strong, but only as traces when conflicting influences are present. It adds that ideas of beauty vary among peoples and cultures.

passages.chapterTitle: Characteristics of the Twelve Signs
passages.text: soils, the varied phenomena on the way, the climatic conditions, the presence or absence of watery surfaces, hills, valleys, dales, mountains, vegetation, animals, birds, beasts, reptiles, the human habitations their varied features, his own physical and mental changes, all these and many more necessarily change his mind, and make him miserable or pleasurable, according to these various influences. Similarly when a planet enters Mesha he will be affected in the 30 degrees with various sources of beneficial and malefic influences. Say the Sun enters Mesha in the 1st degree. We will explain the various influences in our colloquial language. First he enters a friendly house, second he enters his sign of exaltation. Third he enters his own hora, fourth he enters Kuja Drekkana, fifth he enters Kuja Navamsa, he travels in two and quarter stars in each sign which have their own peculiar influences. Aswini extends over 13⅓ degrees and it does not exercise the same influence all through those degrees. The tenth degree or the end of the 3rd quarter is his deep exaltation where he is alleged to give the highest beneficial influence.
passages.summary: The book compares a planet moving through a sign to a traveller affected by changing surroundings, and explains, using the Sun entering Mesha, how the house, exaltation, hora, drekkana, navamsa and constellation each influence it, with deepest exaltation at the tenth degree.

passages.chapterTitle: Characteristics of the Twelve Signs
passages.text: Till the 10th degree he is in the ascendent and reaches the highest point in the 10th degree. From the 11th degree he is said to be in the descent, and gradually loses his powers. When he reaches the 30th degree he loses his power of exaltation and when he enters the 1st degree of Vrishabha, he comes to an unfriendly territory. From the 13⅓ degree to the 26⅔ degree, he will be in Bharani which is quite different in nature, in its results from those of Aswini. Bharani has Yama as its Deity and has its influence. From the 26⅔ degree till he passes the 30th degree or the end of the first quarter of Krithika he travels in a star governed by Agni. Bharani is governed by Yama or the dread judge, who punishes all wicked people after their death. These are not easy lessons which could be learnt by casual glances. They require deep intelligent and patient study.
passages.summary: The book explains that the Sun gains strength up to the 10th degree of Mesha and then declines, entering unfriendly Vrishabha after the 30th degree, and that it passes through constellations ruled by different deities. It stresses that this needs deep, patient study.

passages.chapterTitle: The Sun, Moon, Mars and Mercury in the Twelve Houses
passages.text: Here, the results of the various planets occupying the different Bhavas are sketched out and the astrologer will see how each house and its significations are affected and modified.
passages.summary: The book introduces the chapter, which sets out the results of the planets placed in the different houses and how each house's meanings are changed by them.

passages.chapterTitle: The Sun, Moon, Mars and Mercury in the Twelve Houses
passages.text: The balancing of evidence and pronouncing of correct judgment are not such great difficulties to judge as the balancing of the results of the occupations of the planets in the different houses and making correct predictions for an astrologer. Take Mesha. First there are the influences of the sign. Then we have the Hora, Drekkana, Navamsa, Dwadasamsa, Thrimsamsa, the stellar, and the planetary influences. All these and the influences of combinations, aspects, debilitations, exaltations, retrogrades, accelerations, friendly and unfriendly houses, Moola thrikonas and other particulars will have to be taken into consideration. Any brain however intelligent it may be reels back at the stupendous labour which lies before it in astrological calculations. It is surprising how educated people themselves discontented with their heavy incomes can make up their minds to overlook the dignity of the herculean labour and offer to the really learned astrologers small sums often even less than the humble wages of a street cooly. Such however is the logic of the learned and they have the audacity to find fault with the astrologers for false predictions. This is something like jeering at an Engineer for not building a tank bund properly when he is paid ten rupees for a work which really costs a thousand. What would be his reply readers can answer.
passages.summary: The book says weighing the results of planets in the houses is harder than judging evidence in court, because the sign, its many divisions, the stars, aspects, dignities and other factors must all be considered. It complains that educated people pay learned astrologers very little for this great labour and then blame them for wrong predictions, comparing this to blaming an underpaid engineer.

passages.text: Results have been explained from the constellations lunar influences, sign peculiarities, influences of planets in the different Bhavas. These are specially applicable to females. In astrology as well as in other sciences right judgment is a great factor, weighing of evidence is important. Great patience and labour are wanted. Chandra enters Mesha twelve times a year. Each month has its own peculiar influence, and the various angels he forms both with reference to himself and also for other planets are factors which have to be taken into consideration in delineating the character of women. So also for other planets
passages.summary: The book sums up that results have been given from the constellations, lunar influences, signs and planets in the houses, all specially applicable to women. It stresses that sound judgment, weighing of evidence, patience and labour are needed, and that the Moon's monthly passage and the angles it forms with itself and other planets must be considered, as for the other planets.

passages.text: If Guru is in Lagna, if Chandra is in 7th or in his own vergas, and Sukra is in 10th, the woman will become the wife of a king or of a ruler,
passages.summary: The book says that with Jupiter in the ascendant, the Moon in the 7th house or in its own divisions, and Venus in the 10th, the woman will become the wife of a king or ruler.

passages.text: Here it means that although a girl may be born in humble circumstances and belong to a lower caste than that of the ruler, she will become his wife.

passages.chapterTitle: Rajayogas, or Combinations for Power and Prosperity
passages.text: Beauty is no doubt a powerful weapon for woman to conquer men, but sometimes love is blind, and a woman of ordinary complexion and beauty will be courted by a ruler, under what we may call lucky and other subtle influences. A fair woman sometimes courts and enjoys a dark and repulsive man and a fair man falls in desperate love with a dirty and ugly looking wench. Why and wherefore nobody can satisfactorily explain. Lovers do not see the petty follies they commit.
passages.summary: The book remarks that beauty helps a woman win men, but love is blind, and an ordinary-looking woman may be courted by a ruler through luck and subtle influences; attraction often cannot be explained.

passages.chapterTitle: Rajayogas, or Combinations for Power and Prosperity
passages.text: Sovereignty over the three worlds, Swarga, Martya and Patala has been casually mentioned in the Puranas, but from the Pandavas downwards we have no historical evidence to show that any king has had jurisdiction over the three worlds. Arjuna went to Swarga and fought there. Vikramaditya went into Indraloka and got his valuable Throne with 32 steps guarded by 32 celestial Nymphs to whom are ascribed 32 beautiful interesting and highly romantic stories, which form the theme of a separate book, called Dwatrimsat Sala Bhanjika Kathas.
passages.summary: The book notes that rule over the three worlds (heaven, earth and the underworld) appears in the Puranas, but there is no historical evidence of any king holding it since the Pandavas; it recalls Arjuna's journey to heaven and Vikramaditya's throne with its 32 nymphs and their stories.

passages.chapterTitle: Rajayogas, or Combinations for Power and Prosperity
passages.text: Vimana is derived from the Sanskrit, Vi excessive or high and Mana measure speed and refers to Aeroplanes and all those machines which could travel in the aerial regions. See Verse 48 1st Kanda Amara. Vyomni means aerial regions and that which can fly there is a Vimana. Those cars which contain Devatas are Vimanas. Vina Pakshina Manamuha [?] Gamanay [?], or that which when flying resembles a winged bird.
passages.summary: The book explains that the word Vimana comes from Sanskrit roots meaning high speed and refers to aeroplanes and other flying machines, including cars carrying gods, that fly like a winged bird.

passages.chapterTitle: Rajayogas, or Combinations for Power and Prosperity
passages.text: Swarga is inhabited by Devatas, headed by Indra. Martya is inhabited by human beings who are subjected to Mri to die or death. Patala is inhabited by the Nagas or serpentlike beings headed by Audisesha.
passages.summary: The book explains that heaven is inhabited by the gods under Indra, the earth by mortal humans, and the underworld by serpent beings under Adisesha.

passages.chapterTitle: Rajayogas, or Combinations for Power and Prosperity
passages.text: Royal power is no doubt very covetable and desirable when people have got steady heads and pure minds. They can do a great deal of good. But when they have weak or impulsive temperaments they will plunge themselves into the vortex of sexual and sensual pleasures, and become physically as well as morally ruined.
passages.summary: The book comments that royal power is desirable for steady, pure-minded people who can do much good, but those of weak or impulsive temperament sink into sensual pleasures and are ruined physically and morally.

passages.chapterTitle: Rajayogas, or Combinations for Power and Prosperity
passages.text: much better. Such is the constitution of human society. These Rajayogas give power, money and luxuries afforded by them. But moral and spiritual considerations are different and these have generally fewer chances of access to the royal palaces, than the vices, which not only have better access, but are fondled with great care and loved by the aristocrats. Nemesis deals out its iron hand, catches them in its grip and gives them plenty of diseases and a wonderful variety of sorrows. Palaces are nobly built, richly furnished and present very inviting appearances to outlookers, but when one enters into its precincts, the rotten smell of diseases, social scandals, immoral impulses and horrid forms of vicious and unrighteous deeds hails the outsider and makes him reflect that his humble home is far better than the guilded compartments, enclosing rotten human beings. In the above Rajayogas the virtuous conduct of the women is specially mentioned so that the holy may be distinguished from the unholy, and the healthy from the rotten.
passages.summary: The book comments that royal combinations give power, money and luxury, but vices find easier entry into palaces than morality, bringing disease and sorrow; it says the women's virtuous conduct is specially mentioned to distinguish the good from the corrupt.

passages.text: marries such a woman or one who is born to such a woman may reap the highest blessings No gem can adorn a man or woman, more than their love, morality and chastity The present combinations of planets are driving out such human beings, year after year into the back ground Material civilisation accounts much for this state Earn money by any means is the motto
passages.summary: The book says whoever marries such a woman, or one born to her, may reap the highest blessings, and that love, morality and chastity are the finest adornments. It laments that such people are becoming rarer, blaming material civilisation and the pursuit of money.

passages.chapterTitle: Soubhagya Yogas, or Long Married Life
passages.text: For a respectable, loving, chaste and modest woman, nothing can be more dreadful than the loss of her lawful lord, and this is specially held in great fear among the higher caste Hindu women For an adulterous unsympathetic, immoral and quarrelsome girl, nothing can give her greater pleasure than the death of her husband at an early age This event gives her greater liberty and license for her immoral behaviour and independent conduct and she will be only too glad to do what she likes Widowhood, therefore is an event, which is looked at from various mentalities I give here the most formidable combinations for the widowhood We know there are some angelic and modest women who love their husbands more than a Deity and we also know there are some who treat their husbands with the greatest contempt There are some dirty women, who conspire with their lovers, and poison and kill their husbands There are some godly women, who cannot brook the idea of widowhood, and even kill themselves before their husbands Human Psychology is a great puzzle
passages.summary: The book discusses how widowhood is viewed differently by different women, from dread to welcome, and introduces its combinations for widowhood, mentioning women who harm their husbands and women who would die before them.
